Key Activities: Supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using quantitative statistical data analysis methods, such as: data wrangling, validation, mining, and visualization (in R/RStudio, Python, SQL, Java, JavaScript or another software), as well as software development, application of machine/deep learning and artificial intelligence techniques for problem solving.

Analyses statistical data using established data management methods.  Drafts summary analysis of qualitative and/or quantitative data and presents findings and recommendations to colleagues and/or team members.
Organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies.  Establishes and maintains work files.
Attends Departmental meetings, and interdepartmental and stakeholder meetings (as required), to gather data/information and to optimize the business value of data.
Participates in project teams and working groups to support data management, research and analysis, and other unit activities.

technical activities, skills, responsibi: Judgement is required to conduct non-routine data research, assess the relevance and reliability of the data sources and to organize and consolidate findings.  Some judgement is required to select and apply established methods, as appropriate.

The data preparation and analysis supports the work of studies and projects and the development of reports and recommendations presented to management by senior data analysts. The results can impact the quality of the data analysis used by more senior analysts or project leaders.
Judgement to discuss business information without divulging confidential information.
Participates on project teams and working groups and provides assistance to new employees, as required.
May perform administrative tasks to support the unit in the conduct of studies, the organization and coordination of meetings and other unit activities.

Personal use and care of a computer and related software; standard office equipment, furnishings and supplies; reference material and policy documents; and multimedia equipment. May handle sensitive materials.
Uses taxi chits and travel credit cards for authorized business purposes.

Conducts research and collects data from a variety of sources, aggregating it so that it provides valid and reliable data on which to perform quantitative, retrospective and predictive analysis that measures the impact of the Department’s programs to support evidence-based policy and program decisions.

Apply data science principles including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization, and exploratory/confirmatory, predictive analysis, regression, and qualitative analysis, to clarify the implications of analyses for the department’s policies and programs.

Review data collections and information sources to determine the usefulness of existing sources and assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified methodologies, to identify and evaluate problems in the processing, editing, compilation and presentation of analytical materials.

Participate in research and analytics projects for the design, development and implementation of analytic techniques, including artificial intelligence models and data visualization to enhance Statistics Canada’s data assets and support the evolution of analytics, reporting processes and data governance capabilities that generate more meaningful data in support of both operational and strategic, and program and policy decision making.
Create and test data and mathematical models for bias, of particular importance in predictive and prescriptive analytics.

Key Activities: Develops and coordinates the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, capture, coding and processing of data.
Reviews data inconsistency and integrity problems, recommends new approaches and resolves reporting and respondent relations issues.
Evaluates changes in statistical needs of clients, as well as trends and developments in data collection, capture, coding and processing.
Provides advisory and consultative services to users regarding collection and production efficiency and/or quality.
Participates as a statistical operations representative on teams and working groups throughout the department.
Leads project teams involved in the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data.

Communication: Provides information and advice to managers, employees and the general public on the development, operation and use of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results.

Discusses requirements with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others to establish and elaborate the framework and conditions within which statistical operations will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.

Writes and presents subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify operational systems and processes and/or describe program results for data suppliers and users who may not be familiar with the subject matter or systems processes.
Prepares and explains specifications and guidelines to be used by others in developing and operating systems and processes.
Participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and working groups in order to share knowledge within the area of operational expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of current or emerging economic and/or social issues relating to the program area, in order to identify and resolve data collection and production problems as well as quality issues.

Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data in order to manage, control and improve survey collection, capture, coding and processing activities.

Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to manage the design, development, testing, maintenance and implementation of processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and use databases.
Knowledge of high level programming language, utility programs and/or statistical packages in order to retrieve and manipulate data.
Knowledge of project and time management methods, practices and techniques to develop work plans, estimate resource requirements and to monitor and report on work progress.
Knowledge of the principles and practices of human and financial resource management is required to lead project teams.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of divisional and departmental mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures to order to coordinate and manage on-going operational activities and/or special projects.
Knowledge of divisional operating systems and requirements in order implement and maintain operational systems and applications.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada related to the area of expertise in order to identify potential sources of information for development and operations and/or special studies and to identify and evaluate possible data conflicts.

Knowledge of contacts within key client departments to establish a liaison, to understand and interpret program and user need for statistical data, and to provide advice and guidance on program concepts, methods, techniques and results.
Knowledge of collection/respondent relations as it pertains to the specific program area.
Knowledge of products and services provided by suppliers/vendors is required to evaluate and recommend the purchase of new equipment and/or software.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to data suppliers, users and others with respect to the collection, capture, coding and processing of data. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data  provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Reviews the sources of information, statistical techniques, methods and approaches used in the collection, capture, coding and processing of data within an area of specialty in order to recommend and implement improvements.

Evaluates trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and techniques and recommends improvements. Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, capture, coding and processing methods and procedures used, and their compatibility with other statistical programs.

Interprets the relative quality of data produced, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevancy in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.
Investigates client requirements for statistical information and the suitability of existing data products and services.

Analysis is required to understand and interpret program and user needs for statistical information and translate them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request. Clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with statistical options, methods and techniques available.

Positions.Position Title: Regional Geographer and Management Information Systems Analyst
Key Activities: Conducts delineation of census assignments to support Census operations for the assigned region for all collection activities. Identifies Field Operations Manager (FOM) boundaries. Receives, verifies, sorts and distributes collection maps to the field.

Acts as the subject matter expert within the region for geography-related issues; resolves geo-coding and boundary issues; seeks solutions to atypical problems through consultation with the National Geographer; and provides updates on the progress of delineation activities at the regional and local level.
Receives and responds to queries from managers and staff such as the identification of Census Field Office (CFO) or Crew Leader District (CLD) boundaries.
Delivers training and/or information sessions on interpretation of MIS reports, geography and supports collectives concepts to managers and field staff.
Participates in the evaluation and debriefing process of the Census operation in respect to geography and MIS and collective dwelling enumeration.

Responds to requests from RCC or CFO’s for information and generates MIS Key Indicator Reports (KIR) and MIS detailed reports dealing with various Census tasks including, but not limited to, Geospatial reports, Recruiting, Pay, NRFU, List/Leave, Collectives and Reserves.

Analyzes MIS reports for CFO, RCC and Census Management and provides explanations on reporting processes as required; identifies inconsistencies and investigates and resolves problems; advises management and clients on the quality, reliability, nature and availability of data; and extracts data from MIS reports and KIRs to prepare customize reports, graphs, tables, charts using spreadsheets or databases.
Accesses and utilizes the Collection Management system (CMP) and the MIS Portal to obtain the MIS data sought by various levels of Census management.

Organizes and coordinates collective dwelling data collection activities and builds a regional database of collective organizations (i.e. community assisted group homes, military bases and hospitals) using historical data from previous censuses and information gathered from web-based information systems; creates planning calendars, in-house reports and various types of spreadsheets for collective dwelling enumeration.

Communication: Liaises with the MIS Team (Head Office, FOP) and National Geographer, seeks solutions to atypical situations and provides briefings on the progress of studies/activities undertaken at the local level.

Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology related to geography, geo-coding and boundary issues in order to explain and clarify their application.
Provides advice to managers and staff on matters relating to geography and geo-coding concepts. There is a need to adapt technical terminology for various audiences.

Provides training to users throughout the area on effective data entry, retrieval and reporting techniques and practices and to managers, colleagues and other users within the CFOs on the interpretation of MIS reports and geographic concepts.

Provides assistance with MIS reports, data collection, retrieval and reporting systems, provides instruction and guidance to authorized users on solutions to data entry, coding and report production issues.
Reconciles the Collective Dwelling Listing File (CDLF) with the mail out address file to avoid duplication and prevent incorrect enumeration methods being applied to collective dwellings.

Contacts large and medium sized collective organizations such as health care facilities, military establishments and universities in advance of census collection activities to obtain their cooperation and ensure their full understanding of collection procedures and Statistics Canada’s expectations; answers any questions and resolves outstanding issues with respect to collection procedures prior to the start of collection; identifies contacts to assist with enumeration and obtain building access.
Liaises with Regional Communications staff to obtain publicity services and other special letters and materials required to support collective enumeration activities.
Follows up on complaints and questions from respondents, collective dwelling administrators and MPs.

The incumbent initiates contact with private and public establishments to persuade and obtain their cooperation in providing occupancy records and the access required for collective dwelling enumeration activities.

The incumbent follows up and resolves complaints and answers questions from respondents and external dwelling administrators as well as MPs’ offices to explain requirements and provide clarification on procedures in regard to collective dwelling enumeration.

The incumbent also consults and liaises on daily basis with CFOs and where appropriate RCC managers and staff; works collaboratively with colleagues in other units; provides advice and recommendations in regard to collective dwelling collection requirements and makes recommendations on how to resolve difficult collection targeted strategies. The incumbent deals with the general public when participating in promotional activities.
The incumbent deals primarily with managers and colleagues of the RCC and CFO and provides information and instruction on the use, capability and analysis of MIS reports.
Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of current or emerging geomatics engineering technology methods, techniques and practices in order to identify subject-matter concept and definition requirements, and to conduct studies. This knowledge is used to support the National Geographer in the delivery of geography services to the Census Field Offices within the Region; receive, verify, sort and distribute collection maps to the field; act as the subject matter expert within the region for geography-related issues; resolve geo-coding and boundary issues; and deliver training courses and/or information sessions to managers.

Knowledge of methods and techniques of working within a government environment is required to coordinate and implement collection activities to support the operations of CFOs located within the assigned RCC; to review and recommend work methods, procedures, and support the training of Collective dwelling enumeration activities; to interpret and apply administrative procedures, standards and policies; to provide advice and expertise to CFOs in regard to enumeration requirements; and to resolve problems.
Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the Census Program within Statistics Canada in order to support census operations within an assigned region, conduct studies and to identify and evaluate data conflicts.

Knowledge of contacts within key client departments to establish working relationships; to understand need for geography-related data, and to provide advice and guidance on subject-matter concepts, methods, techniques and results.

Knowledge of the RCC’s mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures to order to coordinate and organize on-going operational activities and/or special projects. Knowledge of CFOs, RCC and Statistics Canada’s mandate, goals, programs and operating and administrative procedures is required in order to clarify directives, guidelines and provide expertise on the use of Collective dwelling systems, procedures and concepts;; plan and coordinate enumeration activities; and apply and ensure compliance to administrative policies and procedures.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the retrieval, editing, validation and dissemination of data. The incumbent must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.

Knowledge of the roles and responsibilities of other functional areas within the RCC such as Communications in order to liaise with Regional Communications to obtain collection publicity services and other special promotional requests for CFOs.

Working knowledge of data collection policies and procedures and relevant sections of administrative legislation such as but not limited to the Privacy Act, Access to Information, Official Languages Act and Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA) as it relates to the collection of data. This knowledge is acquired through continuing study of bulletins and departmental communiqués as well as attending internal training sessions. This knowledge is required to coordinate collection activities and provide advice and support to CFOs on the resolution of issues.
Research and analysis: Analyzes geo-coding and boundary issues and presentation methods and procedures to: identify mailable areas; identify CFO boundaries; validate CU boundaries including CU refine; and delineate assignments for CLs, FOSs, FOMs and Area Managers for all collection activities including L/L, NRFU, E-NRFU, Collectives, Early Enumeration, Canvasser, Reserves, and provide expert advice on adjustments required.

Compiles geography and geo-coding data to produce tables and other output. Summarizes and describes the meaning of information gathered. Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness.
Interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required.

Key Activities: As part of the area management team, organizes, oversees and controls CSU activities within the assigned area for a 7-day collection operation.

Manage and supervise employees hired under the Public Service Employment Act (PSEA); oversee the recruitment, appointment and training of CSU staff and ensure that sufficient staff levels are maintained in the CSU at all times; and deliver training to CSU staff, supervisors and officers.

Monitor and evaluate the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of CSU data collection systems and processes; analyze and produce reports on the progress of the CSU activities; and resolve problems
Including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes.
Respond to and resolve complaints; and contribute to public relations activities to promote census communications and respondent cooperation.

Provide support to regional administration with the opening of the office space such as visits during construction fit-up, ensure office readiness for the beginning of field activities as well as closing down the CSU once operations have been completed.

technical activities, skills, responsibi: Effort is required to make decisions/recommendations on: the determination and definition of objectives, content and approaches for census collection activities in the CSU and the operational framework and conditions within which the statistical program will occur; data collection and transmission processes; the resolution of complaints and problems related to survey participation and non-respondents; the development and distribution of guidelines, instructions and procedures for use by CSU staff; approval of appointments of all Statistics Act staff in the CSU; the assurance that financial expenditures and resources are within allocated budgets; and the day-to-day management of financial, human and material resources of the CSU.
Review and interpret the methods, concepts, techniques and practices applied in the operation of existing systems and processes
Analyze and produce reports on the progress of the CSU activities and resolves problems including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes.

Conduct comprehensive evaluations to determine the effectiveness and efficiency of collection operations. Identify trends, gaps and inconsistencies, and makes recommendations for consideration by Headquarter operations on areas requiring improvements or approaches to be adopted.

Respond orally and in writing to inquiries from managers and employees to provide information and advice on the operation and use of systems and processes, and to provide briefings on CSU program results.
Respond orally and in writing to inquiries from the general public on the requirements for response, purpose of the census or issues with employees.

Intervene and deal with uncooperative and sometimes hostile respondents. There is a requirement to 'take control' over these emotionally-charged situations, and persuade the respondent to take a more rational approach to a situation.
Resolve and negotiate problems, which includes identifying the need for the development, modification and adaptation of operational processes.

Judgment, tact and flexibility are exercised in finding solutions that meet a range of business needs. Decisions/recommendations taken affect the efficient and effective operations of the CSU and the CSU’s compliance to the Statistics Act and agency policies and procedures.
